ford|ranger.title: Crank angle sensor failure

ford|ranger.title: DPF issues on short trips

ford|ranger.title: V6 camshaft sprocket can fracture (REC-006341)

ford|ranger.checkTip: Check the VIN on vehiclerecalls.gov.au and ask for proof the recall work (REC-006341) was done.

ford|ranger.title: Transmission can shift into Park (REC-005759 / REC-006541)
ford|ranger.detail: If battery voltage drops, the electronic shifter may select Park below 6 km/h. The original recall was redone in February 2026.
ford|ranger.checkTip: Check the VIN on vehiclerecalls.gov.au and ask for proof the recall work (REC-005759 and REC-006541) was done.

ford|ranger.title: Rear camera may show no image (REC-006358)
ford|ranger.detail: A software fault can blank the rear camera image (campaign 25S49).
ford|ranger.checkTip: Check the VIN on vehiclerecalls.gov.au and ask for proof the recall work (REC-006358) was done.

ford|ranger.title: Driver seatbelt assembly recall (REC-005639)

ford|territory.title: Front lower ball joint failure

holden|captiva.title: Automatic transmission wear
holden|captiva.detail: The automatic transmission in earlier Captivas can wear and shift harshly if fluid changes have been neglected, though generally less catastrophically than the later facelifted generation.
holden|captiva.checkTip: Test drive for smooth, prompt gear changes and ask about transmission service history.

holden|captiva.title: Electrical faults
holden|captiva.detail: Similar to the later generation but generally less severe, some owners report minor electrical or sensor issues.
holden|captiva.checkTip: Check the dashboard for warning lights and test all electrical accessories.

holden|captiva.title: Diesel injector or turbo wear on high-km examples
holden|captiva.detail: The early diesel engine can develop injector or turbo wear on high-mileage examples, though it does not carry the same severe timing chain reputation as the later 2.2L unit.
holden|captiva.checkTip: Check for excessive smoke on acceleration and ask about service history.

holden|captiva.title: Timing chain failure on 2.2L diesel engine
holden|captiva.detail: The 2.2L diesel engine fitted to most facelifted Captivas is widely and repeatedly reported to suffer premature timing chain stretch or failure, often well before 100,000km, which can destroy the engine and require a full replacement. This is one of the most consistently reported major faults for any used SUV in the Australian market.
holden|captiva.checkTip: Ask specifically whether the timing chain has ever been replaced or inspected, listen closely for rattling from the engine on cold start-up, and strongly consider a specialist pre-purchase inspection given the very high cost if this fault is present.

holden|captiva.title: Automatic transmission failure
holden|captiva.detail: The 6-speed automatic transmission is commonly reported to fail unexpectedly, sometimes with little warning, and replacement is expensive.
holden|captiva.checkTip: Test drive extensively, including at varying speeds and up hills, feeling for hesitation, slipping, or harsh shifts. Ask for full transmission service history.

holden|captiva.title: Turbocharger failure on diesel models
holden|captiva.detail: The turbocharger on diesel models is reported to fail more often than is typical for the class, sometimes linked to the wider engine reliability problems in this generation.
holden|captiva.checkTip: Check for excessive smoke on acceleration, whining noises from the turbo, or a noticeable loss of power.

holden|captiva.title: Frequent electrical faults and warning lights
holden|captiva.detail: Owners very commonly report a range of electrical gremlins - random dashboard warning lights, sensor faults, and general electrical unreliability - contributing heavily to this generation's poor overall reputation.
holden|captiva.checkTip: Start the car cold and check the dashboard for any warning lights, and ask the seller whether warning lights come on intermittently during normal driving.

holden|captiva.title: Overall reliability significantly below class average
holden|captiva.detail: Independent reliability surveys and consumer bodies in Australia have repeatedly rated this generation of Captiva among the least reliable SUVs sold new in the market, with many owners reporting multiple unrelated faults rather than just one issue.
holden|captiva.checkTip: Budget for a thorough independent mechanical inspection before buying, given the unusually high rate of reported problems, and ask for a complete service and repair history.

holden|colorado.title: Timing chain wear and oil consumption if servicing neglected
holden|colorado.detail: The 3.0L 4JJ1 diesel can suffer timing chain wear and oil consumption, particularly when oil changes have been missed.

holden|colorado.title: 6-speed automatic torque converter shudder
holden|colorado.detail: The 6-speed automatic is well known for torque converter shudder (a rumble-strip vibration at light throttle around 60-80 km/h), worse when towing. A new converter costs roughly $1,500-3,500.
holden|colorado.checkTip: Test drive at light throttle between 40 and 80 km/h and feel for shudder; ask whether the torque converter has been replaced.

holden|colorado.title: DPF blockages on short trips
holden|colorado.detail: The 2.8L Duramax DPF can clog on short urban trips when regeneration can't complete.
holden|colorado.checkTip: Ask about typical use and check for DPF warning lights.

holden|colorado.title: Injector faults (rough idle or misfire)

mazda|bt-50.title: Dual-mass flywheel and clutch wear
mazda|bt-50.detail: Manual versions can wear the dual-mass flywheel and clutch, especially with towing or stop-start use.

mazda|bt-50.title: Oil pump failure (original vane-type pump)
mazda|bt-50.detail: The variable-flow vane-type oil pump on the 2.2L and 3.2L diesels can lose its prime if the oil drains for more than about 10 minutes at a service or the ute sits for a long time, starving the engine of oil. Both engines use a timing chain, not a belt. Many owners fit a geared aftermarket pump.
mazda|bt-50.checkTip: The oil light should go out within 3-4 seconds of starting. Ask whether the pump has been upgraded and who services it.

mazda|bt-50.title: EGR cooler failure
mazda|bt-50.detail: EGR cooler failures are a known fault on these diesels and can cause coolant loss, white smoke or overheating.
mazda|bt-50.checkTip: Check the coolant level and history of top-ups, look for white smoke, and ask whether the EGR cooler has been replaced.

mazda|bt-50.title: 6-speed automatic faults (transmission cooler, lead frame)
mazda|bt-50.detail: The 6-speed automatic (6R80) is known for lead frame (internal wiring/speed sensor) faults causing harsh shifts, missing gear display or limp mode (codes P0720-P0723), plus radiator-integrated transmission cooler failures and torque converter clutch shudder. A lead frame fix is roughly $900-1,500.
mazda|bt-50.checkTip: Scan for P07xx codes, test drive at 60-90 km/h on light throttle feeling for shudder, and ask about lead frame or converter replacement.

mazda|bt-50.title: Split intercooler hose or turbo boost loss
mazda|bt-50.detail: Intercooler hoses can split or blow off, causing sudden power loss and warning lights; turbo faults are also reported on high-km examples.
mazda|bt-50.checkTip: Test under hard acceleration and towing load for sudden power loss, and check for oily residue around intercooler hoses.

mitsubishi|challenger.title: Overheating and head gasket failure (pre-March 2014 builds)
mitsubishi|challenger.detail: Tritons with the 2.5L 4D56 diesel built before 18 March 2014 can lose coolant and overheat because the top of the engine block was machined too rough, letting combustion gas and coolant past the head gasket. Mitsubishi's free service campaign 020116 (Nov 2014) fitted a 127 kPa radiator cap, 50% coolant and an ECU update that limits power if coolant is lost. It's a mitigation, not a cure: many engines were replaced under warranty or goodwill, and some owners got no help once out of warranty.
mitsubishi|challenger.checkTip: Read the engine number (engines from 4D56 UCFA9504 onwards have the improved block). Look for a radiator cap marked 127 kPa, and ask for the campaign 020116 record and any engine-replacement invoice. Check the coolant bottle for oil or level loss and ask a mechanic for a combustion-gas (block) test; a short test drive won't reveal it.

mitsubishi|outlander.title: CVT judder, hesitation or failure
mitsubishi|outlander.detail: The continuously variable transmission can judder, hesitate or slip, particularly from a standstill or under load.
mitsubishi|outlander.checkTip: Test drive in stop-start traffic and up a hill; feel for shudder, flaring revs or hesitation, and ask whether CVT fluid has been changed.

mitsubishi|outlander.title: Minor timing chain or engine noise on high-km examples

mitsubishi|outlander.title: Infotainment glitches

mitsubishi|outlander.checkTip: Test the touchscreen and Apple CarPlay/Android Auto connection.

mitsubishi|outlander.title: Early software or charging quirks on PHEV models
mitsubishi|outlander.detail: Some early examples of the redesigned PHEV system have been reported to have minor software or charging behaviour quirks, generally resolved with updates.
mitsubishi|outlander.checkTip: Test the charging function if possible and ask if any software updates have been applied.

mitsubishi|outlander.title: Limited long-term data given how new the model is

mitsubishi|pajero.title: Cracked cylinder head
mitsubishi|pajero.detail: This diesel is known to crack its cylinder head, especially if overheated or worked hard.
mitsubishi|pajero.checkTip: Check for coolant loss, overheating and white smoke.

mitsubishi|pajero.title: Timing belt replacement overdue
mitsubishi|pajero.detail: This engine uses a rubber timing belt that must be replaced on schedule; if it breaks, engine damage is likely.
mitsubishi|pajero.checkTip: Ask for proof of timing belt replacement at the scheduled interval, or budget for it straight away.

mitsubishi|pajero.title: Body and chassis rust
mitsubishi|pajero.detail: Older examples, particularly those used near the coast or off-road, can rust in the chassis, floors and wheel arches.
mitsubishi|pajero.checkTip: Inspect the chassis, floor pans, sills and wheel arches for rust.

mitsubishi|pajero.title: Injector seal leaks ('black death')
mitsubishi|pajero.detail: The 3.2L DI-D diesel's injector seals can leak, causing carbon build-up, ticking and rough running.
mitsubishi|pajero.checkTip: Look for black carbon around the injectors and listen for ticking.

mitsubishi|pajero.title: Body and chassis rust
mitsubishi|pajero.detail: Older examples, particularly those used near the coast or off-road, can rust in the chassis, floors and wheel arches.
mitsubishi|pajero.checkTip: Inspect the chassis, floor pans, sills and wheel arches for rust.

mitsubishi|pajero.title: Injector seal leaks ('black death')

mitsubishi|pajero.title: Automatic transmission wear
mitsubishi|pajero.detail: The automatic can develop harsh shifts or shudder, especially with towing.
mitsubishi|pajero.checkTip: Test drive for harsh shifts or shudder.

mitsubishi|pajero sport.title: DPF blockages on short trips
mitsubishi|pajero sport.detail: Mostly short-trip or city driving can stop the diesel particulate filter from completing its cleaning cycle, causing warning lights and reduced power.
mitsubishi|pajero sport.checkTip: Ask about typical use (city vs highway) and check for DPF warning lights on the test drive.

mitsubishi|pajero sport.title: No major model-specific faults widely reported
mitsubishi|pajero sport.detail: This generation has a good reliability record. Condition, kilometres and service history matter more than any specific known fault.
mitsubishi|pajero sport.checkTip: Check the service history, look for accident repairs and test all features before buying.

mitsubishi|triton.title: Chassis and tray rust
mitsubishi|triton.detail: Like most utes of this age, high-mileage or coastal-use Tritons from this era can develop rust on the chassis and tray.
mitsubishi|triton.checkTip: Inspect underneath for rust on the chassis rails and around the tray mounting points.

mitsubishi|triton.title: General high-km wear on clutch and suspension
mitsubishi|triton.detail: Many of these Tritons were used as work vehicles, so clutches, leaf springs, and bushes can be well worn.
mitsubishi|triton.checkTip: Check for a high or spongy clutch bite point and inspect the rear leaf springs for sagging.

mitsubishi|triton.title: Turbo failures on the 2.5L diesel
mitsubishi|triton.detail: Some owners report turbocharger failures on the 2.5L diesel engine, sometimes linked to oil supply or maintenance issues.
mitsubishi|triton.checkTip: Look for excessive smoke on acceleration and ask about service history, particularly oil change intervals.

mitsubishi|triton.title: Automatic transmission shudder
mitsubishi|triton.detail: Some owners report a mild shudder or hesitation from the automatic transmission, particularly at low speed.
mitsubishi|triton.checkTip: Test drive at low speed and around town to feel for hesitation or shudder.

mitsubishi|triton.title: Overheating after high-load driving
mitsubishi|triton.detail: A service bulletin covers coolant loss through repeated evaporation after high-load driving such as towing.
mitsubishi|triton.checkTip: Check the coolant level and radiator cap rating, and ask about overheating history.

mitsubishi|triton.title: Suction control valve (SCV) faults
mitsubishi|triton.detail: The fuel pump suction control valve on the 3.2L diesel can cause surging, stalling and limp mode.
mitsubishi|triton.checkTip: Watch for idle hunting or stalling and scan for codes.

mitsubishi|triton.title: Recalls: rear axle U-bolts, ball joints
mitsubishi|triton.detail: ML recalls cover rear axle U-bolts (2006-07) and ball joints that could detach (built Oct 2006 - Jan 2009).
mitsubishi|triton.checkTip: Check the VIN on vehiclerecalls.gov.au and ask for proof the recall work (Mitsubishi ML recalls) was done.

mitsubishi|triton.title: Chassis bending behind the cab
mitsubishi|triton.detail: Chassis rails can bend behind the cab when heavy loads sit behind the rear axle.
mitsubishi|triton.checkTip: Check the cab-to-tub gap and the chassis rails behind the cab.

mitsubishi|triton.title: No transmission cooler on some 2009 autos
mitsubishi|triton.detail: Owners report 2009 ML autos without a transmission cooler, which can overheat when towing.
mitsubishi|triton.checkTip: Check whether an external transmission cooler is fitted if it's been towing.

mitsubishi|triton.title: Turbo failures on the 2.5L diesel
mitsubishi|triton.detail: Some owners report turbocharger failures on the 2.5L diesel engine, sometimes linked to oil supply or maintenance issues.
mitsubishi|triton.checkTip: Look for excessive smoke on acceleration and ask about service history, particularly oil change intervals.

mitsubishi|triton.title: Automatic transmission shudder
mitsubishi|triton.detail: Some owners report a mild shudder or hesitation from the automatic transmission, particularly at low speed.
mitsubishi|triton.checkTip: Test drive at low speed and around town to feel for hesitation or shudder.

mitsubishi|triton.title: Timing belt replacement overdue
mitsubishi|triton.detail: The 2.5L 4D56 diesel uses a timing belt that must be replaced on schedule.
mitsubishi|triton.checkTip: Ask for proof of timing belt replacement, or budget for it.

mitsubishi|triton.title: Overheating and head gasket failure (pre-March 2014 builds)
mitsubishi|triton.detail: Tritons with the 2.5L 4D56 diesel built before 18 March 2014 can lose coolant and overheat because the top of the engine block was machined too rough, letting combustion gas and coolant past the head gasket. Mitsubishi's free service campaign 020116 (Nov 2014) fitted a 127 kPa radiator cap, 50% coolant and an ECU update that limits power if coolant is lost. It's a mitigation, not a cure: many engines were replaced under warranty or goodwill, and some owners got no help once out of warranty.
mitsubishi|triton.checkTip: Read the engine number (engines from 4D56 UCFA9504 onwards have the improved block). Look for a radiator cap marked 127 kPa, and ask for the campaign 020116 record and any engine-replacement invoice. Check the coolant bottle for oil or level loss and ask a mechanic for a combustion-gas (block) test; a short test drive won't reveal it.

mitsubishi|triton.title: Chassis bending behind the cab
mitsubishi|triton.detail: Chassis rails can bend behind the cab or over the rear axle when heavy loads sit behind the axle (canopies, water tanks, tow hitch loads, airbag suspension).
mitsubishi|triton.checkTip: Check the gap between cab and tub is even, look along the chassis rails behind the cab for kinks or fresh paint, and ask how it was loaded.

mitsubishi|triton.title: Recalls: front propshaft weld, lamp switch, power seat
mitsubishi|triton.detail: MN recalls include a front propeller shaft weld (MY12), a lamp switch connector (2016) and a power seat short circuit on GLS/GLX-R double cabs (2007-2013).
mitsubishi|triton.checkTip: Check the VIN on vehiclerecalls.gov.au and ask for proof the recall work (Mitsubishi MN recalls) was done.

mitsubishi|triton.title: Turbo oil leaks and early injector failure
mitsubishi|triton.detail: Some owners report turbo oil leaks and injector failures on the 2.5L diesel.
mitsubishi|triton.checkTip: Look for oil around the turbo and smoke on acceleration.

mitsubishi|triton.title: Automatic transmission shudder or hesitation
mitsubishi|triton.detail: A reasonably common owner-reported issue is the automatic transmission shuddering or hesitating at low speed, particularly when the torque converter locks up.
mitsubishi|triton.checkTip: Drive at a steady low speed (around 40-60km/h) and feel for shudder or surge from the transmission.

mitsubishi|triton.title: DPF blockages on short trips
mitsubishi|triton.detail: As with other modern diesel utes, mostly short-trip or city driving can clog the diesel particulate filter.
mitsubishi|triton.checkTip: Ask about typical use and check for DPF warning lights on the test drive.

mitsubishi|triton.title: Front suspension or steering component wear
mitsubishi|triton.detail: Some owners report earlier-than-expected wear in front suspension components such as ball joints or sway bar links.
mitsubishi|triton.checkTip: Have a mechanic check the front suspension and steering components, and listen for clunking over bumps.

mitsubishi|triton.title: Manual gearbox jumping out of gear
mitsubishi|triton.detail: Some 6-speed manuals grind or jump out of 1st to 3rd gear.
mitsubishi|triton.checkTip: Test all gears under load, including a hill start.

mitsubishi|triton.title: Genuine towbar bolt recall
mitsubishi|triton.detail: Genuine towbar mounting bolts could loosen (recall March 2016).
mitsubishi|triton.checkTip: Check the VIN on vehiclerecalls.gov.au and ask for proof the recall work (Mitsubishi MQ towbar recall) was done.

mitsubishi|triton.title: DPF blockages on short trips
mitsubishi|triton.detail: Mostly city or short-trip use can still clog the diesel particulate filter.
mitsubishi|triton.checkTip: Ask about typical usage and check for DPF warning lights.

mitsubishi|triton.title: Clutch wear on manual models used for towing
mitsubishi|triton.detail: Manual models used for regular towing can wear through the clutch earlier than expected.
mitsubishi|triton.checkTip: Check the clutch bite point and ask if the vehicle has been used for regular towing.

mitsubishi|triton.title: Infotainment glitches
mitsubishi|triton.detail: Some owners report occasional freezing or restarting of the touchscreen infotainment system.
mitsubishi|triton.checkTip: Test the touchscreen, Apple CarPlay/Android Auto, and reversing camera during your inspection.

mitsubishi|triton.title: DPF blockages on short trips

mitsubishi|triton.detail: This model is relatively new, so long-term faults may not have shown up yet.
mitsubishi|triton.checkTip: Check for outstanding recalls or software updates and confirm remaining factory warranty.

nissan|350z.title: Oil consumption
nissan|350z.detail: Some VQ35 engines (especially 2005-2006 'rev-up') use excessive oil.
nissan|350z.checkTip: Check the oil level and ask how much it uses.

nissan|350z.title: Modification and hard-use history
nissan|350z.detail: These are popular with enthusiasts, so many have been modified, tuned, raced or drifted, which shortens engine, gearbox and clutch life.
nissan|350z.checkTip: Look for aftermarket parts, check for a compliance/engineering certificate on modifications, and get a compression test and specialist inspection.

nissan|dualis.title: CVT judder or failure
nissan|dualis.detail: This model shares its platform and CVT transmission with the equivalent-era X-Trail and Qashqai, and is commonly reported to judder, hesitate, or fail under load.
nissan|dualis.checkTip: Test drive including some hills or hard acceleration and feel for shuddering or whining from the transmission. Ask for CVT service history.

nissan|dualis.title: Timing chain rattle
nissan|dualis.detail: The petrol engine shared with related models from this era can develop timing chain guide or tensioner rattle over time.
nissan|dualis.checkTip: Listen for a rattling noise from the engine on cold start-up.

nissan|dualis.title: General reliability concerns tied to early CVT examples
nissan|dualis.detail: Being an early adopter of CVT technology in this class, overall reliability is generally rated below later Nissan CVT-equipped models.
nissan|dualis.checkTip: Get a thorough independent mechanical inspection before buying, particularly focused on the transmission.

nissan|elgrand.title: Automatic transmission wear
nissan|elgrand.detail: The automatic can wear with age.
nissan|elgrand.checkTip: Check for slipping or harsh shifts.

nissan|elgrand.title: Power sliding door faults
nissan|elgrand.detail: Power sliding door motors, cables and sensors can fail, leaving doors stuck or slow.
nissan|elgrand.checkTip: Open and close each power door several times.

nissan|juke.title: Dual-clutch transmission hesitation or shudder
nissan|juke.detail: The dual-clutch automatic can hesitate when pulling away, shudder at low speed or shift jerkily in traffic.
nissan|juke.checkTip: Test drive in stop-start traffic, crawl forward slowly and pull away briskly from a stop; feel for shudder, clunks or delays.

nissan|juke.title: Limited long-term reliability data
nissan|juke.detail: This model is relatively new, so long-term faults may not have shown up yet.
nissan|juke.checkTip: Check for outstanding recalls or software updates and confirm remaining factory warranty.

nissan|leaf.title: Battery capacity loss in hot climates
nissan|leaf.detail: Early Leaf batteries have no active cooling and lose capacity quickly in hot climates, reducing range significantly.
nissan|leaf.checkTip: Check the battery health bars on the dash (or get an app/scan report) and test real-world range.

nissan|leaf.title: Limited range for older 24 kWh batteries
nissan|leaf.detail: Early 24 kWh Leafs had modest range when new; with degradation, real-world range may be well under 100 km.
nissan|leaf.checkTip: Test real-world range and check battery health bars.

nissan|leaf.title: Battery capacity loss in hot climates
nissan|leaf.detail: Early Leaf batteries have no active cooling and lose capacity quickly in hot climates, reducing range significantly.
nissan|leaf.checkTip: Check the battery health bars on the dash (or get an app/scan report) and test real-world range.

nissan|leaf.title: Battery overheating and fast-charge throttling
nissan|leaf.detail: The battery has no active cooling, so repeated fast charging can heat it and slow charging speeds; capacity loss is faster in hot climates.
nissan|leaf.checkTip: Check battery health and ask about fast-charging habits.

nissan|maxima.detail: This generation has a good reliability record. Condition, kilometres and service history matter more than any specific known fault.

nissan|murano.checkTip: Test drive in stop-start traffic and up a hill; feel for shudder, flaring revs or hesitation, and ask whether CVT fluid has been changed.

nissan|murano.title: CVT judder, hesitation or failure
nissan|murano.detail: The continuously variable transmission can judder, hesitate or slip, particularly from a standstill or under load.
nissan|murano.checkTip: Test drive in stop-start traffic and up a hill; feel for shudder, flaring revs or hesitation, and ask whether CVT fluid has been changed.

nissan|navara.title: Timing chain and VP44 fuel pump failure (pre-2008 ZD30 3.0L diesel)
nissan|navara.detail: The early 3.0L ZD30DDTi turbo-diesel used before around 2008 is the D22's biggest known weak point, with a documented pattern of premature timing chain stretch and VP44 fuel pump failure - later D22s switched to the more common-rail YD25 2.5L diesel, which does not share this reputation.
nissan|navara.checkTip: Confirm which engine is fitted (ZD30 3.0L vs YD25 2.5L) and, on ZD30 examples, ask specifically about timing chain and VP44 fuel pump history.

nissan|navara.title: EGR clogging on YD25 2.5L diesel
nissan|navara.detail: On the later YD25 2.5L diesel, carbon build-up in the EGR system is a common finding past 100,000km, causing rough idle, power loss, and black smoke.
nissan|navara.checkTip: Check for rough idling, hesitation, or excess smoke on acceleration, particularly on higher-mileage examples.

nissan|navara.title: Chassis and tray rust
nissan|navara.detail: Being an older, often work-use ute, rust on the chassis and tray is a common finding.
nissan|navara.checkTip: Get underneath with a torch and check the chassis rails and tray mounts for rust.

nissan|navara.title: Clutch wear on high-km work vehicles
nissan|navara.detail: Many D22 Navaras were used as work vehicles, so clutches can be well worn on high-mileage examples.
nissan|navara.checkTip: Check the clutch bite point and ask about the vehicle's work history.

nissan|navara.title: Timing chain rattle on petrol and diesel engines
nissan|navara.detail: The YD25's timing chain can stretch, rattle and then jump or snap, destroying the engine; failures from around 70,000 km are reported. It mainly affects Spanish-built (VIN starting VSK) ST-X models from 2005-2010; Thai-built (VIN MNT) and later engines are reported to be better. Duplex chain conversion kits are common.
nissan|navara.checkTip: Check the VIN prefix (VSK = Spain, MNT = Thailand), listen for rattle on a cold start, and ask for any chain replacement or duplex conversion invoice.

nissan|navara.title: DPF issues on facelifted diesel models
nissan|navara.detail: Later diesel D40s fitted with a diesel particulate filter can clog if mostly driven on short trips.
nissan|navara.checkTip: Ask about typical use and check for DPF warning lights.

nissan|navara.title: Rear tray and chassis rust
nissan|navara.detail: As with most work-use utes of this age, rust on the tray and chassis is a common finding.
nissan|navara.checkTip: Check underneath and around the tray for rust.

nissan|navara.title: Low-mounted radiator damage
nissan|navara.detail: The radiator's bottom tank sits below the front crossmember and gets damaged off-road.
nissan|navara.checkTip: Inspect the radiator and underbody protection.

nissan|navara.title: CV joint failure
nissan|navara.detail: The independent front suspension's CV joints wear quickly with off-road use.
nissan|navara.checkTip: Check CV boots and listen for clicking on full lock.

nissan|navara.title: Chassis corrosion
nissan|navara.detail: Chassis rust is one of the biggest D40 risks.

nissan|navara.title: Rough idle or DPF issues on 2.3L twin-turbo diesel
nissan|navara.detail: The 2.3L twin-turbo diesel can develop DPF clogging or rough idling if mostly used for short trips around town.
nissan|navara.checkTip: Ask about typical use and check for warning lights and a smooth, steady idle.

nissan|navara.title: Automatic transmission shudder or harsh shifting
nissan|navara.detail: Some owners of the 7-speed automatic report shudder or harsh shifting, particularly at low speed.
nissan|navara.checkTip: Test drive with several stop-start situations and feel for shudder or harsh gear changes.

nissan|navara.title: Timing chain noise on some early engines
nissan|navara.detail: Some early examples of the 2.3L diesel have been reported to develop timing chain noise.
nissan|navara.checkTip: Listen for rattling from the engine on cold start-up.

nissan|navara.title: Rear coil spring sag
nissan|navara.detail: Dual cabs with coil-sprung rear suspension sag under canopies or towing, with light, vague steering; Series 2 got stiffer springs. Leaf-sprung single and king cabs aren't affected.
nissan|navara.checkTip: Measure rear ride height and look for bump-stop marks.

nissan|navara.title: Rough idle or DPF issues on 2.3L twin-turbo diesel
nissan|navara.detail: The 2.3L twin-turbo diesel can develop DPF clogging or rough idling if mostly used for short trips around town.
nissan|navara.checkTip: Ask about typical use and check for warning lights and a smooth, steady idle.

nissan|navara.title: Automatic transmission shudder or harsh shifting
nissan|navara.detail: Some owners of the 7-speed automatic report shudder or harsh shifting, particularly at low speed.
nissan|navara.checkTip: Test drive with several stop-start situations and feel for shudder or harsh gear changes.

nissan|navara.title: Timing chain noise on some early engines
nissan|navara.detail: Some early examples of the 2.3L diesel have been reported to develop timing chain noise.
nissan|navara.checkTip: Listen for rattling from the engine on cold start-up.

nissan|note.detail: This generation has a good reliability record. Condition, kilometres and service history matter more than any specific known fault.
nissan|note.checkTip: Check the service history, look for accident repairs and test all features before buying.

toyota|camry.checkTip: Ask for proof of timing belt replacement at the scheduled interval, or budget for it straight away.

toyota|camry.title: Automatic transmission wear
toyota|camry.detail: The 4-speed automatic can slip with age.

toyota|camry.title: Engine oil sludge
toyota|camry.detail: The 3.0L 1MZ-FE V6 is prone to oil sludge if oil changes are stretched, which can destroy the engine.
toyota|camry.checkTip: Look under the oil filler cap for sludge and ask for oil-change history.

toyota|camry.title: Timing belt replacement overdue
toyota|camry.detail: This engine uses a rubber timing belt that must be replaced on schedule; if it breaks, engine damage is likely.
toyota|camry.checkTip: Ask for proof of timing belt replacement at the scheduled interval, or budget for it straight away.

toyota|camry.title: Automatic transmission wear on high-mileage examples
toyota|camry.detail: Being an older, high-mileage vehicle by now, the automatic transmission can develop hesitation or harsh shifting if fluid changes have been neglected.
toyota|camry.checkTip: Ask for transmission service history and test drive for smooth, prompt gear changes.

toyota|camry.title: Rust in older, coastal-use examples
toyota|camry.detail: As with most cars this age, rust can develop in wheel arches, sills, and the boot floor, especially in coastal areas.
toyota|camry.checkTip: Check wheel arches, sills, and the boot floor for rust or bubbling paint.

toyota|camry.title: General age-related wear
toyota|camry.detail: Suspension bushes, engine mounts, and other wear items are common on a car this age.
toyota|camry.checkTip: Have a mechanic check suspension bushes and engine mounts.

toyota|camry.title: Oil consumption on 2.4L four-cylinder engines (2AZ-FE)
toyota|camry.detail: The 2.4L 2AZ-FE engine used in this generation is a well-documented case of excessive oil consumption from worn piston rings - the same engine and issue affects the equivalent-era RAV4, and has been the subject of class-action litigation overseas. Left unchecked it can lead to serious engine damage.
toyota|camry.checkTip: Check the oil level before and after a test drive, ask for a full oil top-up history, and be wary of any burnt-oil smell or blue exhaust smoke on start-up.

toyota|camry.title: Automatic transmission shudder
toyota|camry.detail: Some owners report a mild shudder or hesitation from the automatic transmission, particularly when cold.
toyota|camry.checkTip: Test drive with the engine cold and warm and feel for shudder or hesitation.

toyota|camry.title: Generally reliable with only minor items reported
toyota|camry.detail: This generation has a strong reliability reputation overall, with mostly minor items reported.
toyota|camry.checkTip: Focus your inspection on service history and general wear rather than specific known faults.

toyota|camry.title: Hybrid battery degradation on very high-mileage examples
toyota|camry.detail: On hybrid models with very high mileage, the hybrid battery pack can gradually lose capacity, slightly reducing fuel economy or electric-only performance.
toyota|camry.checkTip: Ask about hybrid battery health, check for a hybrid system warning light, and watch the dash for battery charge behaviour during the test drive.

toyota|camry.title: Infotainment or electrical glitches
toyota|camry.detail: Some owners report occasional minor electrical or infotainment quirks.
toyota|camry.checkTip: Test the infotainment screen, air conditioning, and all electrical accessories.

toyota|camry.title: Fuel pump failure (2013-2015 and 2017 builds)
toyota|camry.detail: Some 50-series Camrys built September 2013-June 2015 or from September 2017 fall within Toyota Australia's genuine, ACCC-listed low-pressure fuel pump recall, where a deformed impeller can stop the pump working and cause a stall.
toyota|camry.checkTip: Ask whether this fuel pump recall has been completed - Toyota's recall helpline (1800 987 366) or any Toyota dealer can check against the VIN.

toyota|camry.title: General reliability strong
toyota|camry.detail: This generation is regarded as very reliable overall, with few widespread mechanical issues reported.
toyota|camry.checkTip: Focus your inspection on service history rather than specific known faults.

toyota|camry.title: 12V battery drain if left unused (Hybrid)
toyota|camry.detail: The small 12V auxiliary battery can drain if the car sits unused for an extended period, occasionally leaving it unable to start.
toyota|camry.checkTip: Ask how regularly the car is driven and confirm it starts promptly without a jump-start.

toyota|camry.title: Infotainment glitches
toyota|camry.detail: Some owners report occasional freezing or slow response from the touchscreen infotainment system.
toyota|camry.checkTip: Test the touchscreen and Apple CarPlay/Android Auto connection.

toyota|camry.title: Very few widespread issues reported
toyota|camry.detail: This generation has an excellent reliability reputation so far, with no major common faults identified.
toyota|camry.checkTip: Focus your inspection on service history and general condition.

toyota|camry.title: Limited long-term reliability data
toyota|camry.detail: This model is relatively new, so long-term faults may not have shown up yet.
toyota|camry.checkTip: Check for outstanding recalls or software updates and confirm remaining factory warranty.

toyota|celica.title: Oil consumption
toyota|celica.detail: The 1.8L 1ZZ-FE can use excessive oil, and the 2ZZ-GE's lift bolt can fail if over-revved.
toyota|celica.checkTip: Check oil level and ask about consumption.

toyota|celica.title: Modification and hard-use history
toyota|celica.detail: These are popular with enthusiasts, so many have been modified, tuned, raced or drifted, which shortens engine, gearbox and clutch life.
toyota|celica.checkTip: Look for aftermarket parts, check for a compliance/engineering certificate on modifications, and get a compression test and specialist inspection.

toyota|corolla.title: Oil consumption and wear on very high-mileage engines
toyota|corolla.detail: Being an older, high-mileage vehicle by now, minor oil consumption and general engine wear are common, though the engines are generally very robust.
toyota|corolla.checkTip: Check the oil level and condition, and ask about service history including timing belt replacement.

toyota|corolla.title: Rust in coastal or high-moisture areas
toyota|corolla.detail: As with most cars this age, rust can develop in wheel arches, sills, and the boot floor, especially in coastal areas.
toyota|corolla.checkTip: Check wheel arches, sills, and the boot floor for rust or bubbling paint.

toyota|corolla.title: Oil consumption on some engines
toyota|corolla.detail: Some four-cylinder Corollas from this era can burn oil faster than normal due to piston ring wear, which if unchecked can lead to engine damage.
toyota|corolla.checkTip: Check the oil level before and after a test drive, and ask about oil consumption history.

toyota|corolla.title: General age-related wear
toyota|corolla.detail: Suspension bushes, mounts, and other wear items are common on a car this age.
toyota|corolla.checkTip: Have a mechanic check suspension bushes and mounts for wear.

toyota|corolla.title: Minor oil consumption on some engines
toyota|corolla.detail: Some examples can use a bit more oil than expected, though generally less pronounced than the previous generation.
toyota|corolla.checkTip: Check the oil level and ask about oil top-up history.

toyota|corolla.title: General wear items
toyota|corolla.detail: As with any Corolla of this age, suspension bushes and other wear items may need attention.
toyota|corolla.checkTip: Have a mechanic check suspension components.

toyota|corolla.title: CVT hesitation or judder at low speed
toyota|corolla.detail: Some CVT-equipped E170 Corollas are reported to hesitate or judder slightly at low speed, particularly pulling away from a stop.
toyota|corolla.checkTip: Test drive with several stop-start situations and feel for hesitation or judder.

toyota|corolla.title: Generally reliable with only minor items reported
toyota|corolla.detail: This generation is regarded as very reliable overall, with mostly minor items like cabin trim rattles reported.
toyota|corolla.checkTip: Listen for cabin rattles over rough roads.

toyota|corolla.title: Fuel pump failure (2017-2018 builds)
toyota|corolla.detail: Some E170 Corollas built in the 2017-2018 window fall within Toyota Australia's genuine, ACCC-listed low-pressure fuel pump recall, where a deformed impeller can stop the pump working and cause a stall.
toyota|corolla.checkTip: Ask whether this fuel pump recall has been completed - Toyota's recall helpline (1800 987 366) or any Toyota dealer can check against the VIN.

toyota|corolla.title: CVT hesitation or judder at low speed
toyota|corolla.detail: Some CVT-equipped E170 Corollas are reported to hesitate or judder slightly at low speed, particularly pulling away from a stop.
toyota|corolla.checkTip: Test drive with several stop-start situations and feel for hesitation or judder.

toyota|corolla.title: Generally reliable with only minor items reported
toyota|corolla.detail: This generation is regarded as very reliable overall, with mostly minor items like cabin trim rattles reported.
toyota|corolla.checkTip: Listen for cabin rattles over rough roads.

toyota|corolla.title: Fuel pump failure (2017-2018 builds)
toyota|corolla.detail: Some E170 Corollas built in the 2017-2018 window fall within Toyota Australia's genuine, ACCC-listed low-pressure fuel pump recall, where a deformed impeller can stop the pump working and cause a stall.
toyota|corolla.checkTip: Ask whether this fuel pump recall has been completed - Toyota's recall helpline (1800 987 366) or any Toyota dealer can check against the VIN.

toyota|corolla.title: Infotainment glitches
toyota|corolla.detail: Some owners report occasional freezing or slow response from the touchscreen infotainment system.
toyota|corolla.checkTip: Test the touchscreen and Apple CarPlay/Android Auto connection.

toyota|corolla.title: 12V battery drain if left unused (Hybrid)
toyota|corolla.detail: As with other Toyota hybrids, the small 12V auxiliary battery can drain if the car sits unused for an extended period.
toyota|corolla.checkTip: Ask how regularly the car is driven and confirm it starts promptly without a jump-start.

toyota|corolla axio / fielder.title: CVT judder, hesitation or failure
toyota|corolla axio / fielder.detail: The continuously variable transmission can judder, hesitate or slip, particularly from a standstill or under load.
toyota|corolla axio / fielder.checkTip: Test drive in stop-start traffic and up a hill; feel for shudder, flaring revs or hesitation, and ask whether CVT fluid has been changed.

toyota|corolla axio / fielder.title: Check import history and odometer
toyota|corolla axio / fielder.detail: Most examples are Japanese imports; check import records and odometer history.

toyota|corolla axio / fielder.title: Hybrid battery ageing
toyota|corolla axio / fielder.detail: The high-voltage hybrid battery loses capacity with age and kilometres; replacement is expensive, though reconditioned packs are available.
toyota|corolla axio / fielder.checkTip: Ask for a hybrid battery health check, watch for hybrid warning lights and poorer fuel economy.

toyota|corolla axio / fielder.title: CVT judder, hesitation or failure
toyota|corolla axio / fielder.detail: The continuously variable transmission can judder, hesitate or slip, particularly from a standstill or under load.
toyota|corolla axio / fielder.checkTip: Test drive in stop-start traffic and up a hill; feel for shudder, flaring revs or hesitation, and ask whether CVT fluid has been changed.

toyota|echo.title: No major model-specific faults widely reported
toyota|echo.detail: This generation has a good reliability record. Condition, kilometres and service history matter more than any specific known fault.
toyota|echo.checkTip: Check the service history, look for accident repairs and test all features before buying.

toyota|fortuner.title: DPF fails to complete regeneration (white smoke, foul smell)
toyota|fortuner.detail: 2.8L 1GD and 2.4L 2GD diesels acquired between 1 October 2015 and 23 April 2020 suffered widespread DPF problems (white smoke, foul smell, blocked filters). The Federal Court found them defective, and a $750m class action settlement was announced in October 2026, still subject to court approval. Settlement payments don't pass to someone buying the vehicle now.
toyota|fortuner.checkTip: Ask for proof of Toyota's free 2020 DPF fix, check for white smoke or a foul exhaust smell, and look for DPF warning lights.

toyota|fortuner.title: Fifth injector (DPF dosing injector) faults
toyota|fortuner.detail: The exhaust fifth injector used for DPF regeneration can clog or fail.

toyota|gr86.title: Limited long-term reliability data
toyota|gr86.detail: This model is relatively new, so long-term faults may not have shown up yet.
toyota|gr86.checkTip: Check for outstanding recalls or software updates and confirm remaining factory warranty.

toyota|harrier.title: Excessive oil consumption
toyota|harrier.detail: The 2.4L 2AZ-FE four-cylinder is known for oil consumption on some engines, and head bolt threads can strip, causing coolant leaks.
toyota|harrier.checkTip: Check the oil level, ask how much oil it uses and check for coolant loss.

toyota|harrier.title: Hybrid brake actuator failure
toyota|harrier.detail: The electronically controlled brake actuator can leak internally and fail, triggering ABS/brake warnings and a pump that runs constantly; it is costly to replace.
toyota|harrier.checkTip: Check for brake/ABS warning lights and listen for the brake pump running or buzzing excessively.

toyota|harrier.title: No major model-specific faults widely reported
toyota|harrier.detail: This generation has a good reliability record. Condition, kilometres and service history matter more than any specific known fault.
toyota|harrier.checkTip: Check the service history, look for accident repairs and test all features before buying.

toyota|hiace.title: Cracked cylinder heads (diesel)
toyota|hiace.detail: Older 1KZ-TE and 3L diesels can crack cylinder heads, especially if overheated.
toyota|hiace.checkTip: Check for coolant loss and overheating, and ask about head repairs.

toyota|hiace.title: Body and chassis rust
toyota|hiace.detail: Older examples, particularly those used near the coast or off-road, can rust in the chassis, floors and wheel arches.
toyota|hiace.checkTip: Inspect the chassis, floor pans, sills and wheel arches for rust.

toyota|hiace.title: Injector and copper seat washer failures
toyota|hiace.detail: The KD-series diesels are known for injector faults, including failed copper seat washers, causing rough idle, cold-start knock and white smoke.
toyota|hiace.checkTip: Listen for knocking on a cold start, watch for white smoke and ask whether injectors or seat washers have been replaced.

toyota|hiace.title: High-kilometre commercial use
toyota|hiace.detail: Many have done very high kilometres as work vans or shuttles.

toyota|hiace.title: DPF blockages on short trips
toyota|hiace.detail: Mostly short-trip or city driving can stop the diesel particulate filter from completing its cleaning cycle, causing warning lights and reduced power.
toyota|hiace.checkTip: Ask about typical use (city vs highway) and check for DPF warning lights on the test drive.

toyota|hiace.title: Limited long-term reliability data
toyota|hiace.detail: This model is relatively new, so long-term faults may not have shown up yet.
toyota|hiace.checkTip: Check for outstanding recalls or software updates and confirm remaining factory warranty.

toyota|hilux.title: Chassis and tray rust in coastal areas
toyota|hilux.detail: Older Hilux utes used near the coast or as work trucks can develop rust on the chassis rails, tray, and rear wheel arches, especially without regular underbody cleaning.
toyota|hilux.checkTip: Get underneath with a torch and check the chassis rails, tray mounts, and rear wheel arches for rust bubbling or flaking paint.

toyota|hilux.title: Overdue timing belt service
toyota|hilux.detail: These older engines use a timing belt rather than a chain, and if it isn't replaced on schedule (commonly every 100,000-150,000km) it can snap and cause serious engine damage.
toyota|hilux.checkTip: Ask for service records showing the timing belt was replaced, or budget for it immediately if there's no proof.

toyota|hilux.title: General high-mileage wear from work or towing use
toyota|hilux.detail: Many of these Hilux were used as tradie or farm vehicles, so clutches, leaf springs, and suspension bushes can be well worn by now.
toyota|hilux.checkTip: Check for uneven tyre wear, a sagging rear end, and a clutch that bites very high or low.

toyota|hilux.title: Diesel injector wear on high-km examples
toyota|hilux.detail: The diesel engines from this era can develop worn fuel injectors over very high mileages, leading to rough idling, smoke, or reduced power.
toyota|hilux.checkTip: Listen for a rough or uneven idle and check for excessive smoke on start-up or hard acceleration.

toyota|hilux.title: Clutch and dual-mass flywheel wear
toyota|hilux.detail: Manual versions used hard for towing or work can wear out the clutch and flywheel assembly earlier than expected.
toyota|hilux.checkTip: Feel for shuddering when taking off from a stop, and listen for rattling at idle in neutral.

toyota|hilux.title: Chassis and tray rust
toyota|hilux.detail: As with the earlier model, tray and chassis rust is common on high-mileage or coastal-use examples.
toyota|hilux.checkTip: Inspect the chassis rails and tray mounting points closely for rust.

toyota|hilux.title: Injector and copper seat washer failures
toyota|hilux.detail: The 3.0L 1KD-FTV and 2.5L 2KD-FTV diesels are known for injector faults, including failed copper seat washers, causing rough idle, cold-start knock and white smoke.
toyota|hilux.checkTip: Listen for knocking on a cold start, watch for white smoke and rough idle, and ask whether injectors or seat washers have been replaced.

toyota|hilux.title: Cracked pistons
toyota|hilux.detail: Euro IV 3.0L 1KD-FTV engines from roughly 2007-2012 are known to crack pistons, causing a sudden knock, black smoke and heavy blow-by; the engine is usually finished. Toyota bulletin EG-0008T-0112 introduced revised pistons.
toyota|hilux.checkTip: Check for blow-by at the oil filler cap with the engine running, avoid heavily tuned examples, and ask whether revised pistons have been fitted.

toyota|hilux.title: Timing belt replacement overdue
toyota|hilux.detail: The KD-series diesels use a rubber timing belt, which must be replaced at the scheduled interval.
toyota|hilux.checkTip: Ask for proof of timing belt replacement on schedule, or budget for it.

toyota|hilux.title: EGR carbon build-up
toyota|hilux.detail: Carbon build-up in the EGR system is common on these diesels and can cause rough running and reduced performance.
toyota|hilux.checkTip: Ask whether the EGR system has been cleaned and check for rough running.

toyota|hilux.title: Airbag spiral cable recall (REC-003553)
toyota|hilux.detail: The steering wheel airbag spiral cable could fail and disable the driver airbag (2014 recall).
toyota|hilux.checkTip: Check the VIN on vehiclerecalls.gov.au and ask for proof the recall work (REC-003553) was done.

toyota|hilux.title: DPF fails to complete regeneration (white smoke, foul smell)
toyota|hilux.detail: 2.8L 1GD and 2.4L 2GD diesels acquired between 1 October 2015 and 23 April 2020 suffered widespread DPF problems (white smoke, foul smell, blocked filters). The Federal Court found them defective, and a $750m class action settlement was announced in October 2026, still subject to court approval. Settlement payments don't pass to someone buying the vehicle now.
toyota|hilux.checkTip: Ask for proof of Toyota's free 2020 DPF fix, check for white smoke or a foul exhaust smell, and look for DPF warning lights.

toyota|hilux.title: Fifth injector (DPF dosing injector) faults
toyota|hilux.detail: The exhaust 'fifth injector' used for DPF regeneration can clog or fail, particularly on earlier models. Reported by some owners; not widely documented.
toyota|hilux.checkTip: Ask about DPF/fifth-injector repairs and check for warning lights.

toyota|hilux.title: Timing chain rattle
toyota|hilux.detail: Timing chain rattle has been reported on earlier N80 engines. Reported by some owners; not widely documented.
toyota|hilux.checkTip: Listen for rattling on a cold start.

toyota|hilux.title: Piston 'slap' noise on cold start (2.8L engine)
toyota|hilux.detail: Some N80 Hilux with the 2.8L turbo-diesel make a knocking or slapping noise for a few seconds on a cold start; Toyota has acknowledged this in some cases as a piston design characteristic rather than damage, but it's worth noting. Reported by some owners; not widely documented.
toyota|hilux.checkTip: Start the engine cold, ideally the first start of the day, and listen for a knocking noise that fades after a few seconds.

toyota|hilux.title: Automatic transmission shudder at low speed
toyota|hilux.detail: Some owners report a mild shudder or hesitation from the 6-speed automatic, particularly when cold. Reported by some owners; not widely documented.
toyota|hilux.checkTip: Drive at low speed with light throttle, including pulling away from a stop, and feel for any shudder.

toyota|hilux.title: Airbag recall (REC-001297)
toyota|hilux.detail: HiLuxes built 30 June - 1 December 2015 were recalled because an airbag control chip could deactivate the airbags (not Takata).
toyota|hilux.checkTip: Check the VIN on vehiclerecalls.gov.au and ask for proof the recall work (REC-001297) was done.

toyota|hilux.title: Brake assist recall (REC-001315)
toyota|hilux.detail: Brake assist could be lost if the brake pedal was pumped repeatedly; 2018-2020 HiLux and Fortuner recalled.
toyota|hilux.checkTip: Check the VIN on vehiclerecalls.gov.au and ask for proof the recall work (REC-001315) was done.

toyota|hilux.title: Fuel pump can stall the engine
toyota|hilux.detail: Denso low-pressure fuel pumps fitted from September 2017 could fail and stall the engine (Toyota campaigns 2020).
toyota|hilux.checkTip: Check the VIN on vehiclerecalls.gov.au and ask for proof the recall work (Toyota fuel pump campaign) was done.

toyota|hilux.title: Number plate bracket cracking (REC-005004)
toyota|hilux.detail: The rear plate bracket can crack on rough roads and the plate may fall off (2015-2021 models).
toyota|hilux.checkTip: Check the VIN on vehiclerecalls.gov.au and ask for proof the recall work (REC-005004) was done.

toyota|hilux.title: Limited long-term reliability data
toyota|hilux.detail: This model is relatively new, so long-term faults may not have shown up yet.
toyota|hilux.checkTip: Check for outstanding recalls or software updates and confirm remaining factory warranty.

toyota|hilux.title: Power steering earth connection recall (REC-006578)
toyota|hilux.detail: 13,390 HiLuxes built 28 Aug 2025 - 24 Feb 2026 were recalled for a power steering earth connection fault.
toyota|hilux.checkTip: Check the VIN on vehiclerecalls.gov.au and ask for proof the recall work (REC-006578) was done.

toyota|hilux surf.title: Cracked cylinder head
toyota|hilux surf.detail: This diesel is known to crack its cylinder head, especially if overheated or worked hard.
toyota|hilux surf.checkTip: Check for coolant loss, overheating and white smoke.

toyota|hilux surf.title: Timing belt replacement overdue
toyota|hilux surf.detail: This engine uses a rubber timing belt that must be replaced on schedule; if it breaks, engine damage is likely.
toyota|hilux surf.checkTip: Ask for proof of timing belt replacement at the scheduled interval, or budget for it straight away.

toyota|hilux surf.title: Body and chassis rust
toyota|hilux surf.detail: Older examples, particularly those used near the coast or off-road, can rust in the chassis, floors and wheel arches.
toyota|hilux surf.checkTip: Inspect the chassis, floor pans, sills and wheel arches for rust.

toyota|kluger.title: No major model-specific faults widely reported
toyota|kluger.detail: This generation has a good reliability record. Condition, kilometres and service history matter more than any specific known fault.
toyota|kluger.checkTip: Check the service history, look for accident repairs and test all features before buying.

toyota|kluger.title: VVT-i oil line leak
toyota|kluger.detail: Early 3.5L 2GR-FE V6s used a rubber section in the VVT-i oil feed line that can burst and leak oil rapidly; an all-metal replacement fixes it.
toyota|kluger.checkTip: Ask whether the VVT-i oil line has been replaced with the updated metal line and check for oil leaks.

toyota|kluger.title: Water pump leaks
toyota|kluger.detail: The V6's water pump commonly leaks with age.
toyota|kluger.checkTip: Check coolant level and look for leaks.

toyota|kluger.title: No major model-specific faults widely reported
toyota|kluger.detail: This generation has a good reliability record. Condition, kilometres and service history matter more than any specific known fault.
toyota|kluger.checkTip: Check the service history, look for accident repairs and test all features before buying.

toyota|kluger.title: Limited long-term reliability data
toyota|kluger.detail: This model is relatively new, so long-term faults may not have shown up yet.
toyota|kluger.checkTip: Check for outstanding recalls or software updates and confirm remaining factory warranty.

toyota|landcruiser.title: Front axle and king pin bearing wear
toyota|landcruiser.detail: The solid front axle and king pin bearings can wear over time, especially on vehicles used hard off-road or for heavy towing, leading to steering play or noise.
toyota|landcruiser.checkTip: Check for excessive play in the steering and have the front axle and king pins inspected by a 4x4 specialist.

toyota|landcruiser.title: Turbo and injector wear on high-km V8 diesels
toyota|landcruiser.detail: Very high-mileage V8 diesel engines can develop turbo or injector wear, particularly on vehicles used for heavy towing or remote-area work.
toyota|landcruiser.checkTip: Check for excessive smoke on acceleration and ask about service and towing history.

toyota|landcruiser.title: Clutch wear under heavy load
toyota|landcruiser.detail: As the only transmission option is manual, clutches can wear faster on vehicles regularly used for towing or off-road work.
toyota|landcruiser.checkTip: Check the clutch bite point and ask about towing or heavy-duty use history.

toyota|landcruiser.title: Excessive oil consumption on single-turbo V8
toyota|landcruiser.detail: Early 1VD V8 diesels (mainly 2007-2010 builds) are known for oil consumption; Toyota bulletin EG-0120T-1211 (2011) covers it and revised the vacuum pump. Toyota's allowance is up to 1 L per 1,000 km.
toyota|landcruiser.checkTip: Ask how much oil it uses between services, check the intercooler pipes for oil and look for a catch can. DPF models (from Sep 2016) need low-ash oil.

toyota|landcruiser.title: Body and chassis rust
toyota|landcruiser.detail: Older examples, particularly those used near the coast or off-road, can rust in the chassis, floors and wheel arches.
toyota|landcruiser.checkTip: Inspect the chassis, floor pans, sills and wheel arches for rust.

toyota|landcruiser.title: Front swivel hub leaks and wear
toyota|landcruiser.detail: Front swivel hub seals leak and bearings wear.
toyota|landcruiser.checkTip: Look for oil on the swivel hubs.

toyota|landcruiser.title: Turbo-diesel head cracking
toyota|landcruiser.detail: 1HZ/1HD diesels, especially turbo-converted ones, can crack heads.
toyota|landcruiser.checkTip: Check for coolant loss and overheating.

toyota|landcruiser.title: Air suspension faults on Sahara and other equipped models
toyota|landcruiser.detail: Higher-spec models with air suspension can develop compressor or air line faults over time, causing the vehicle to sit unevenly or fail to self-level.
toyota|landcruiser.checkTip: Check that the vehicle sits level and rises/lowers correctly if fitted with height adjustment, and ask about air suspension service history.

toyota|landcruiser.title: Timing belt replacement overdue
toyota|landcruiser.detail: Both the 4.7L 2UZ-FE V8 and the 4.2L 1HD-FTE turbo-diesel use timing belts that must be replaced on schedule.
toyota|landcruiser.checkTip: Ask for proof of timing belt replacement, or budget for it.

toyota|landcruiser.title: Front differential weakness (IFS models)
toyota|landcruiser.detail: The independent front suspension 100 Series has a smaller front differential that can fail under heavy off-road or towing use; the 105 Series has a solid front axle.
toyota|landcruiser.checkTip: Listen for front diff whine or clunks in 4WD and look for oil leaks.

toyota|landcruiser.title: Timing chain and idler gear wear on early V8 turbo-diesel (200 Series)
toyota|landcruiser.detail: Some early 200 Series V8 turbo-diesels have been reported to develop timing chain or idler gear wear over very high mileages, which can be costly to repair if left unaddressed.
toyota|landcruiser.checkTip: Listen for rattling from the engine on cold start-up and ask for a full service history, particularly any timing component work.

toyota|landcruiser.title: Air suspension faults on Sahara and other equipped models
toyota|landcruiser.detail: Higher-spec models with air suspension can develop compressor or air line faults over time, causing the vehicle to sit unevenly or fail to self-level.
toyota|landcruiser.checkTip: Check that the vehicle sits level and rises/lowers correctly if fitted with height adjustment, and ask about air suspension service history.

toyota|landcruiser.title: DPF issues on later diesel models
toyota|landcruiser.detail: Later 200 Series diesels fitted with a diesel particulate filter can clog if mostly driven on short trips.
toyota|landcruiser.checkTip: Ask about typical use and check for DPF warning lights.

toyota|landcruiser.title: Fuel pump failure (2017-2019 builds)
toyota|landcruiser.detail: 200 Series LandCruisers built between July 2017 and December 2019 were covered by a genuine, ACCC-listed Toyota Australia safety recall for a low-pressure fuel pump whose impeller could deform and stop the pump working, which can cause a stall.
toyota|landcruiser.checkTip: Ask whether this fuel pump recall has been completed - Toyota's recall helpline (1800 987 366) or any Toyota dealer can check against the VIN.

toyota|landcruiser.title: Exhaust fuel-addition injector clogging
toyota|landcruiser.detail: Toyota Australia ran a customer service campaign covering more than 40,000 300 Series LandCruisers built between July 2021 and February 2025, after the exhaust after-treatment fuel-addition injector (part of the diesel particulate filter regeneration system) could become clogged and trigger an 'Engine Maintenance Required' warning.
toyota|landcruiser.checkTip: Ask whether this exhaust injector campaign has been completed, and check for an 'Engine Maintenance Required' warning on the dash during your inspection.

toyota|landcruiser.title: Transmission control software recall
toyota|landcruiser.detail: Toyota Australia issued a safety recall on some 300 Series LandCruisers (and the related Tundra) covering a transmission control unit (ECT-ECU) software reprogram.
toyota|landcruiser.checkTip: Ask the seller or a Toyota dealer whether the transmission ECU software recall has been completed on this specific vehicle, quoting the VIN.

toyota|landcruiser.title: Infotainment glitches
toyota|landcruiser.detail: Some owners report occasional freezing or slow response from the touchscreen infotainment system.
toyota|landcruiser.checkTip: Test the touchscreen, digital instrument cluster, and connected services.

toyota|landcruiser.title: Limited long-term data given how new the model is
toyota|landcruiser.detail: As a relatively new model, long-term reliability patterns are not yet well established.
toyota|landcruiser.checkTip: Focus your inspection on service history and any completed recalls rather than assuming specific wear patterns.

toyota|mark x.title: Carbon build-up on intake valves
toyota|mark x.detail: Direct-injection V6s can build carbon on the intake valves.

toyota|mark x.title: No major model-specific faults widely reported
toyota|mark x.detail: This generation has a good reliability record. Condition, kilometres and service history matter more than any specific known fault.
toyota|mark x.checkTip: Check the service history, look for accident repairs and test all features before buying.

toyota|mr2.title: Modification and hard-use history
toyota|mr2.detail: These are popular with enthusiasts, so many have been modified, tuned, raced or drifted, which shortens engine, gearbox and clutch life.
toyota|mr2.checkTip: Look for aftermarket parts, check for a compliance/engineering certificate on modifications, and get a compression test and specialist inspection.

toyota|mr2.title: Body and chassis rust
toyota|mr2.detail: Older examples, particularly those used near the coast or off-road, can rust in the chassis, floors and wheel arches.
toyota|mr2.checkTip: Inspect the chassis, floor pans, sills and wheel arches for rust.

toyota|mr2.title: Timing belt replacement overdue
toyota|mr2.detail: This engine uses a rubber timing belt that must be replaced on schedule; if it breaks, engine damage is likely.
toyota|mr2.checkTip: Ask for proof of timing belt replacement at the scheduled interval, or budget for it straight away.

toyota|prado.title: Cracked cylinder heads
toyota|prado.detail: The 1KZ-TE 3.0L diesel can crack its cylinder head, especially if overheated.
toyota|prado.checkTip: Check for coolant loss and overheating.

toyota|prado.title: Timing belt replacement overdue
toyota|prado.detail: This engine uses a rubber timing belt that must be replaced on schedule; if it breaks, engine damage is likely.
toyota|prado.checkTip: Ask for proof of timing belt replacement at the scheduled interval, or budget for it straight away.

toyota|prado.title: Body and chassis rust
toyota|prado.detail: Older examples, particularly those used near the coast or off-road, can rust in the chassis, floors and wheel arches.
toyota|prado.checkTip: Inspect the chassis, floor pans, sills and wheel arches for rust.

toyota|prado.title: Injector and copper seat washer failures
toyota|prado.detail: The KD-series diesels are known for injector faults, including failed copper seat washers, causing rough idle, cold-start knock and white smoke.
toyota|prado.checkTip: Listen for knocking on a cold start, watch for white smoke and ask whether injectors or seat washers have been replaced.

toyota|prado.title: Timing belt replacement overdue
toyota|prado.detail: This engine uses a rubber timing belt that must be replaced on schedule; if it breaks, engine damage is likely.
toyota|prado.checkTip: Ask for proof of timing belt replacement at the scheduled interval, or budget for it straight away.

toyota|prado.title: Injector and copper seat washer failures
toyota|prado.detail: The 3.0L 1KD-FTV and 2.5L 2KD-FTV diesels are known for injector faults, including failed copper seat washers, causing rough idle, cold-start knock and white smoke.
toyota|prado.checkTip: Listen for knocking on a cold start, watch for white smoke and rough idle, and ask whether injectors or seat washers have been replaced.

toyota|prado.title: Timing belt replacement overdue
toyota|prado.detail: The KD-series diesels use a rubber timing belt, which must be replaced at the scheduled interval.
toyota|prado.checkTip: Ask for proof of timing belt replacement on schedule, or budget for it.

toyota|prado.title: DPF fails to complete regeneration (white smoke, foul smell)
toyota|prado.detail: 2.8L 1GD and 2.4L 2GD diesels acquired between 1 October 2015 and 23 April 2020 suffered widespread DPF problems (white smoke, foul smell, blocked filters). The Federal Court found them defective, and a $750m class action settlement was announced in October 2026, still subject to court approval. Settlement payments don't pass to someone buying the vehicle now.
toyota|prado.checkTip: Ask for proof of Toyota's free 2020 DPF fix, check for white smoke or a foul exhaust smell, and look for DPF warning lights.

toyota|prado.title: Limited long-term reliability data
toyota|prado.detail: This model is relatively new, so long-term faults may not have shown up yet.
toyota|prado.checkTip: Check for outstanding recalls or software updates and confirm remaining factory warranty.

toyota|prius.title: Hybrid battery ageing
toyota|prius.detail: The high-voltage hybrid battery loses capacity with age and kilometres; replacement is expensive, though reconditioned packs are available.
toyota|prius.checkTip: Ask for a hybrid battery health check, watch for hybrid warning lights and poorer fuel economy.

toyota|prius.title: Hybrid brake actuator failure
toyota|prius.detail: The electronically controlled brake actuator can leak internally and fail, triggering ABS/brake warnings and a pump that runs constantly; it is costly to replace.
toyota|prius.checkTip: Check for brake/ABS warning lights and listen for the brake pump running or buzzing excessively.

toyota|prius.title: Head gasket and EGR issues at high km
toyota|prius.detail: The 1.5L 1NZ-FXE can develop head gasket failures at high kilometres, often linked to EGR problems.
toyota|prius.checkTip: Check coolant level and for rough running.

toyota|prius.title: Oil consumption and head gasket failure
toyota|prius.detail: The 1.8L 2ZR-FXE hybrid engine in this era is known for oil consumption that can lead to EGR clogging and head gasket failure.
toyota|prius.checkTip: Check the oil level, watch for coolant loss and listen for knocking or rough running on a cold start.

toyota|rav4.detail: This engine uses a rubber timing belt that must be replaced on schedule; if it breaks, engine damage is likely.
toyota|rav4.checkTip: Ask for proof of timing belt replacement at the scheduled interval, or budget for it straight away.

toyota|rav4.title: Body and chassis rust
toyota|rav4.detail: Older examples, particularly those used near the coast or off-road, can rust in the chassis, floors and wheel arches.
toyota|rav4.checkTip: Inspect the chassis, floor pans, sills and wheel arches for rust.

toyota|rav4.title: No major model-specific faults widely reported
toyota|rav4.detail: This generation has a good reliability record. Condition, kilometres and service history matter more than any specific known fault.
toyota|rav4.checkTip: Check the service history, look for accident repairs and test all features before buying.

toyota|rav4.title: Engine oil consumption (2.4L engine)
toyota|rav4.detail: Some 2.4L four-cylinder RAV4s from this era are known to burn engine oil faster than normal, which can lead to engine damage if the level isn't checked and topped up regularly.
toyota|rav4.checkTip: Ask for service records showing regular oil level checks, and check the dipstick before and after a test drive to see how much oil has been used.

toyota|rav4.title: Timing chain rattle on V6 models
toyota|rav4.detail: Some V6 versions can develop a rattling noise from a stretched timing chain, especially on cold start.
toyota|rav4.checkTip: Listen for rattling from the engine on a cold start-up.

toyota|rav4.title: General age-related wear
toyota|rav4.detail: Being an older vehicle, wear items like suspension bushes and minor rust in wheel arches are common.
toyota|rav4.checkTip: Have a mechanic check suspension bushes and look for rust around wheel arches and door sills.

toyota|rav4.title: Door lock actuator or handle issues
toyota|rav4.detail: Some owners report door lock actuators or handles becoming unreliable over time.
toyota|rav4.checkTip: Test all door locks and handles, including via the key fob, during your inspection.

toyota|rav4.title: Infotainment glitches
toyota|rav4.detail: Some owners report occasional freezing of the touchscreen infotainment system.
toyota|rav4.checkTip: Test the touchscreen and Bluetooth/Apple CarPlay connection during your test drive.

toyota|rav4.title: 12V battery drain if left unused (Hybrid)
toyota|rav4.detail: The small 12V auxiliary battery can drain if the vehicle sits unused for an extended period, sometimes leaving it unable to start.
toyota|rav4.checkTip: Ask how often the vehicle is driven and check that it starts promptly without needing a jump-start.

toyota|rav4.title: Panoramic sunroof rattle
toyota|rav4.detail: Some owners of sunroof-equipped RAV4s report a rattling noise from the sunroof mechanism over bumps.
toyota|rav4.checkTip: Drive over some rough road sections and listen for rattling from the roof area, with the sunroof closed.

toyota|supra.title: Sequential turbo vacuum hose faults
toyota|supra.detail: Ageing vacuum hoses in the sequential twin-turbo system cause boost problems.
toyota|supra.checkTip: Check for a smooth transition to the second turbo.

toyota|tarago.title: Excessive oil consumption
toyota|tarago.detail: The 2.4L 2AZ-FE four-cylinder is known for oil consumption on some engines, and head bolt threads can strip, causing coolant leaks.
toyota|tarago.checkTip: Check the oil level, ask how much oil it uses and check for coolant loss.

toyota|tarago.title: Excessive oil consumption
toyota|tarago.detail: The 2.4L 2AZ-FE four-cylinder is known for oil consumption on some engines, and head bolt threads can strip, causing coolant leaks.
toyota|tarago.checkTip: Check the oil level, ask how much oil it uses and check for coolant loss.

toyota|tarago.title: VVT-i oil line leak
toyota|tarago.detail: Early 3.5L 2GR-FE V6s used a rubber section in the VVT-i oil feed line that can burst and leak oil rapidly; an all-metal replacement fixes it.
toyota|tarago.checkTip: Ask whether the VVT-i oil line has been replaced with the updated metal line and check for oil leaks.

toyota|tarago.title: Power sliding door faults
toyota|tarago.detail: Power sliding door motors, cables and sensors can fail, leaving doors stuck or slow.
toyota|tarago.checkTip: Open and close each power door several times.

toyota|wish.title: Oil consumption (early 1.8L)
toyota|wish.detail: Early 1ZZ-FE 1.8L engines can use excessive oil.
toyota|wish.checkTip: Check oil level and for blue smoke.

toyota|wish.title: CVT judder, hesitation or failure
toyota|wish.detail: The continuously variable transmission can judder, hesitate or slip, particularly from a standstill or under load.
toyota|wish.checkTip: Test drive in stop-start traffic and up a hill; feel for shudder, flaring revs or hesitation, and ask whether CVT fluid has been changed.

toyota|yaris.title: No major model-specific faults widely reported
toyota|yaris.detail: This generation has a good reliability record. Condition, kilometres and service history matter more than any specific known fault.
toyota|yaris.checkTip: Check the service history, look for accident repairs and test all features before buying.

volkswagen|amarok.title: Timing belt replacement overdue
volkswagen|amarok.detail: The 2.0L TDI and BiTDI diesels use a timing belt that must be replaced on schedule; failures have been reported.
volkswagen|amarok.checkTip: Ask for proof of timing belt replacement at the scheduled interval, or budget for it.

volkswagen|amarok.title: EGR and DPF blockages
volkswagen|amarok.detail: The 2.0L diesels can suffer EGR and DPF blockages, particularly with short-trip use.
volkswagen|amarok.checkTip: Ask about typical use and check for DPF or engine warning lights.

volkswagen|amarok.title: Emissions software recall (EA189 'Dieselgate')
volkswagen|amarok.detail: The 2.0L diesel was part of VW's EA189 emissions scandal and subject to a software/hardware recall.
volkswagen|amarok.checkTip: Ask whether the emissions recall work has been completed and check the dealer service history.

volkswagen|amarok.title: Dual-mass flywheel and clutch wear
volkswagen|amarok.detail: Manual models can wear the dual-mass flywheel and clutch, especially if used for towing.
volkswagen|amarok.checkTip: Check the clutch bite point and listen for rattling in neutral.

volkswagen|amarok.title: Turbo or injector wear on high-km diesels used for towing
volkswagen|amarok.detail: Vehicles used regularly for towing or heavy loads can show earlier turbo or injector wear, leading to smoke or reduced power.
volkswagen|amarok.checkTip: Check for excessive smoke on acceleration and ask about towing history.

volkswagen|amarok.title: Auxiliary belt can shred into the timing belt
volkswagen|amarok.detail: On early 2.0L diesels the auxiliary (serpentine) belt can shred and its fragments get behind the timing cover, destroying the timing belt and engine.
volkswagen|amarok.checkTip: Inspect the auxiliary belt and tensioner, and ask about any timing cover update.

volkswagen|amarok.title: Rear timing chain wear
volkswagen|amarok.detail: The 3.0L V6 TDI's timing chains sit at the rear of the engine; stretch and cold-start rattle are reported from around 160,000-180,000 km, and replacement means removing the gearbox.
volkswagen|amarok.checkTip: Listen for rattling on a cold start.

volkswagen|amarok.title: DPF issues on short-trip use
volkswagen|amarok.detail: As with any modern diesel, mostly short-trip or city driving can lead to diesel particulate filter clogging.
volkswagen|amarok.checkTip: Ask about typical use and check for DPF warning lights.

volkswagen|amarok.title: Infotainment glitches (shared platform with new Ranger)
volkswagen|amarok.detail: Being closely related to the current Ford Ranger, some owners report similar infotainment freezing or connectivity glitches.
volkswagen|amarok.checkTip: Test the touchscreen, Apple CarPlay/Android Auto, and camera systems thoroughly.

volkswagen|amarok.title: Limited long-term data given how new the model is
volkswagen|amarok.detail: As a relatively new model, long-term reliability patterns are not yet well established.
volkswagen|amarok.checkTip: Focus your inspection on service history rather than assuming specific wear patterns.

volkswagen|caddy.title: Emissions software recall (EA189 'Dieselgate')
volkswagen|caddy.detail: This 2.0L or 1.6L TDI diesel was part of VW Group's EA189 emissions scandal and subject to a recall.
volkswagen|caddy.checkTip: Ask whether the emissions recall work has been completed.

volkswagen|caddy.title: 7-speed dry DSG shudder or mechatronic failure
volkswagen|caddy.detail: The 7-speed dry-clutch DSG (DQ200) can shudder, jerk at low speed or suffer mechatronic unit failures.
volkswagen|caddy.checkTip: Crawl forward slowly and pull away from a stop several times; feel for shudder or clunks and ask about DSG repairs.

volkswagen|caddy.title: Timing chain stretch
volkswagen|caddy.detail: Early 1.2L and 1.4L TSI engines are known for timing chain stretch and tensioner problems.
volkswagen|caddy.checkTip: Listen for a rattle on cold start and ask about timing chain replacement.

volkswagen|caddy.title: 7-speed dry DSG shudder or mechatronic failure
volkswagen|caddy.detail: The 7-speed dry-clutch DSG (DQ200) can shudder, jerk at low speed or suffer mechatronic unit failures.
volkswagen|caddy.checkTip: Crawl forward slowly and pull away from a stop several times; feel for shudder or clunks and ask about DSG repairs.

volkswagen|caddy.detail: This generation has a good reliability record. Condition, kilometres and service history matter more than any specific known fault.
