volkswagen|caddy.detail: This model is relatively new, so long-term faults may not have shown up yet.
volkswagen|caddy.checkTip: Check for outstanding recalls or software updates and confirm remaining factory warranty.

volkswagen|golf.title: Timing chain tensioner failure on turbo petrol engines
volkswagen|golf.detail: Some turbocharged petrol engines from this era have a known weak point in the timing chain tensioner, which can fail and cause the chain to jump or engine damage if not addressed.
volkswagen|golf.checkTip: Ask if the timing chain tensioner has been updated or replaced, listen for a rattling noise from the engine on cold start, and get a specialist check if unsure.

volkswagen|golf.title: DSG maintenance and mechatronic issues
volkswagen|golf.detail: DSG-equipped Golfs need regular oil and filter changes for the gearbox, and the mechatronic control unit can develop faults if maintenance is skipped.
volkswagen|golf.checkTip: Ask for records showing DSG service history, and feel for jerkiness or hesitation when driving.

volkswagen|golf.title: Water pump failure
volkswagen|golf.detail: The electric/plastic-impeller water pumps used on some engines of this era are known to fail earlier than a traditional pump.
volkswagen|golf.checkTip: Check for coolant warning lights and ask about water pump service history.

volkswagen|golf.title: Timing chain tensioner failure on turbo petrol engines
volkswagen|golf.detail: Some turbocharged petrol engines from this era have a known weak point in the timing chain tensioner, which can fail and cause the chain to jump or engine damage if not addressed.
volkswagen|golf.checkTip: Ask if the timing chain tensioner has been updated or replaced, listen for a rattling noise from the engine on cold start, and get a specialist check if unsure.

volkswagen|golf.title: DSG maintenance and mechatronic issues
volkswagen|golf.detail: DSG-equipped Golfs need regular oil and filter changes for the gearbox, and the mechatronic control unit can develop faults if maintenance is skipped.
volkswagen|golf.checkTip: Ask for records showing DSG service history, and feel for jerkiness or hesitation when driving.

volkswagen|golf.title: Water pump failure
volkswagen|golf.detail: The electric/plastic-impeller water pumps used on some engines of this era are known to fail earlier than a traditional pump.
volkswagen|golf.checkTip: Check for coolant warning lights and ask about water pump service history.

volkswagen|golf.title: DSG shudder or jerkiness (dry-clutch 7-speed)
volkswagen|golf.detail: Some Mk7 Golfs with the 7-speed dry-clutch DSG are reported to shudder or hesitate at low speed, particularly in stop-start traffic.
volkswagen|golf.checkTip: Test drive in stop-start conditions and feel for shudder or hesitation from the gearbox.

volkswagen|golf.title: Carbon build-up on intake valves
volkswagen|golf.detail: Direct-injection turbo petrol engines like these can build up carbon deposits on the intake valves over time, which may eventually cause rough running and require a cleaning service.
volkswagen|golf.checkTip: Ask if an intake valve clean has ever been done, particularly on high-km examples, and listen for rough idling.

volkswagen|golf.title: Timing chain tensioner (early examples)
volkswagen|golf.detail: Some early Mk7 examples carried over the earlier timing chain tensioner design before a revision, and can suffer the same rattling/failure issue as Mk5/Mk6.
volkswagen|golf.checkTip: Listen for rattling on cold start and ask if the tensioner has been updated.

volkswagen|golf.title: Infotainment and touch-control glitches
volkswagen|golf.detail: The Mk8 Golf's touch-sensitive climate and volume controls, along with the infotainment system, are commonly reported by owners and reviewers to be laggy or glitchy.
volkswagen|golf.checkTip: Spend time operating the touchscreen, climate controls, and steering wheel touch buttons to check they respond reliably.

volkswagen|golf.title: Carbon build-up on intake valves
volkswagen|golf.detail: As with other direct-injection VW engines, carbon can build up on the intake valves over time.
volkswagen|golf.checkTip: Ask about intake valve cleaning history on high-km examples.

volkswagen|golf.title: DSG software glitches
volkswagen|golf.detail: Some owners report occasional software-related hesitations or warning lights from the DSG transmission, often resolved with a dealer software update.
volkswagen|golf.checkTip: Ask if any DSG-related recalls or software updates have been carried out, and test drive for odd behaviour.

volkswagen|passat.title: Timing chain tensioner failure
volkswagen|passat.detail: Early TFSI/TSI timing chain tensioners can fail, letting the chain jump teeth and causing major engine damage.
volkswagen|passat.checkTip: Listen for a rattle on cold start and ask whether the tensioner has been updated.

volkswagen|passat.title: DSG mechatronic or clutch faults
volkswagen|passat.detail: DSG dual-clutch automatics can suffer mechatronic unit or clutch pack faults, causing harsh shifts or warning lights; regular DSG oil changes matter on wet-clutch units.
volkswagen|passat.checkTip: Check for jerky shifts and warning lights, and ask for proof of DSG oil changes.

volkswagen|passat.title: Oil pump drive failure
volkswagen|passat.detail: Some 2.0L TDI pumpe-düse diesels suffer oil pump drive failure, causing sudden loss of oil pressure.
volkswagen|passat.checkTip: Ask whether the oil pump drive has been checked or upgraded.

volkswagen|passat.title: 7-speed dry DSG shudder or mechatronic failure
volkswagen|passat.detail: The 7-speed dry-clutch DSG (DQ200) can shudder, jerk at low speed or suffer mechatronic unit failures.
volkswagen|passat.checkTip: Crawl forward slowly and pull away from a stop several times; feel for shudder or clunks and ask about DSG repairs.

volkswagen|passat.title: Excessive oil consumption
volkswagen|passat.detail: Early EA888 (Gen 2) 1.8L/2.0L TFSI engines are known for excessive oil consumption caused by piston ring design.
volkswagen|passat.checkTip: Check the oil level and ask how much oil it uses between services, and whether pistons or rings have been replaced.

volkswagen|passat.title: Emissions software recall (EA189 'Dieselgate')
volkswagen|passat.detail: This 2.0L or 1.6L TDI diesel was part of VW Group's EA189 emissions scandal and subject to a recall.
volkswagen|passat.checkTip: Ask whether the emissions recall work has been completed.

volkswagen|passat.title: DSG mechatronic or clutch faults
volkswagen|passat.detail: DSG dual-clutch automatics can suffer mechatronic unit or clutch pack faults, causing harsh shifts or warning lights; regular DSG oil changes matter on wet-clutch units.
volkswagen|passat.checkTip: Check for jerky shifts and warning lights, and ask for proof of DSG oil changes.

volkswagen|passat.title: Water pump / thermostat housing coolant leak
volkswagen|passat.detail: The plastic water pump and thermostat housing on EA888 Gen 3 engines commonly leak coolant.
volkswagen|passat.checkTip: Check for coolant loss, a sweet smell or crusty residue around the water pump.

volkswagen|polo.title: Window regulator and electrical faults
volkswagen|polo.detail: Window regulators and minor electrical faults are common.
volkswagen|polo.checkTip: Test all windows and electrical features.

volkswagen|polo.title: No major model-specific faults widely reported
volkswagen|polo.detail: This generation has a good reliability record. Condition, kilometres and service history matter more than any specific known fault.
volkswagen|polo.checkTip: Check the service history, look for accident repairs and test all features before buying.

volkswagen|polo.title: Timing chain stretch
volkswagen|polo.detail: Early 1.2L and 1.4L TSI engines are known for timing chain stretch and tensioner problems.
volkswagen|polo.checkTip: Listen for a rattle on cold start and ask about timing chain replacement.

volkswagen|polo.title: 7-speed dry DSG shudder or mechatronic failure
volkswagen|polo.detail: The 7-speed dry-clutch DSG (DQ200) can shudder, jerk at low speed or suffer mechatronic unit failures.
volkswagen|polo.checkTip: Crawl forward slowly and pull away from a stop several times; feel for shudder or clunks and ask about DSG repairs.

volkswagen|polo.title: 7-speed dry DSG shudder or mechatronic failure

volkswagen|tiguan.title: Timing chain tensioner failure
volkswagen|tiguan.detail: Some turbocharged petrol engines from this era have a known weak point in the timing chain tensioner, which can fail and cause the chain to jump or engine damage if not addressed.
volkswagen|tiguan.checkTip: Ask if the timing chain tensioner has been updated or replaced, and listen for rattling on cold start-up.

volkswagen|tiguan.title: DSG mechatronic issues
volkswagen|tiguan.detail: DSG-equipped Tiguans need regular oil and filter changes for the gearbox, and the mechatronic control unit can develop faults if maintenance is skipped.
volkswagen|tiguan.checkTip: Ask for DSG service records, and feel for jerkiness or hesitation when driving.

volkswagen|tiguan.title: Water pump failure
volkswagen|tiguan.detail: The electric/plastic-impeller water pumps used on some engines of this era are known to fail earlier than a traditional pump.
volkswagen|tiguan.checkTip: Check for coolant warning lights and ask about water pump service history.

volkswagen|tiguan.title: DSG shudder or hesitation
volkswagen|tiguan.detail: Some owners report the dual-clutch transmission shuddering or hesitating at low speed, particularly in stop-start traffic.
volkswagen|tiguan.checkTip: Test drive in stop-start conditions and feel for shudder or hesitation from the gearbox.

volkswagen|tiguan.title: Carbon build-up on intake valves
volkswagen|tiguan.detail: Direct-injection turbo petrol engines can build up carbon deposits on the intake valves over time, which may eventually cause rough running.
volkswagen|tiguan.checkTip: Ask if an intake valve clean has ever been done, particularly on high-km examples.

volkswagen|tiguan.title: Infotainment glitches
volkswagen|tiguan.detail: Some owners report occasional freezing or slow response from the touchscreen infotainment system.
volkswagen|tiguan.checkTip: Test the touchscreen and Apple CarPlay/Android Auto connection.

volkswagen|tiguan.title: Infotainment and touch-control glitches
volkswagen|tiguan.detail: Similar to the latest Golf, the touch-sensitive controls and infotainment system are commonly reported by owners and reviewers to be laggy or glitchy.
volkswagen|tiguan.checkTip: Spend time operating the touchscreen and climate controls to check they respond reliably.

volkswagen|tiguan.title: Limited long-term data given how new the model is
volkswagen|tiguan.detail: As a relatively new model, long-term reliability patterns are not yet well established.
volkswagen|tiguan.checkTip: Focus your inspection on service history rather than assuming specific wear patterns.

volkswagen|touareg.title: Air suspension failure
volkswagen|touareg.detail: Air springs, compressors and valve blocks can fail, causing sagging or warning lights; repairs are expensive.
volkswagen|touareg.checkTip: Check the vehicle sits level after standing, cycle the ride heights and watch for suspension warnings.

volkswagen|touareg.title: Electrical faults and expensive repairs
volkswagen|touareg.detail: Electrical gremlins and expensive drivetrain repairs (especially V10 TDI) are common.
volkswagen|touareg.checkTip: Scan for faults and get a specialist inspection.

volkswagen|touareg.title: DPF blockages on short trips
volkswagen|touareg.detail: Mostly short-trip or city driving can stop the diesel particulate filter from completing its cleaning cycle, causing warning lights and reduced power.
volkswagen|touareg.checkTip: Ask about typical use (city vs highway) and check for DPF warning lights on the test drive.
